label: early input of l/1/m/z/x in sequences starting with d/f/c
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (0.03% of steps). 93% of mass falls in the original phase at positions 3-5 (62% at position 3). It needs several things at once: the first token is d (63% of mass; f and c account for most of the rest), the current input is one of l, 1, m, z, x (l alone carries 47%), and the previous token is one of z, g, w, e, l, o. It is strongest on d ? ? l at position 3 after z/w/g/e (that predicate has precision 0.86 but low recall). It is silent at positions 0-1, on the delimiter, and almost silent in the copy phase, where it gives a few weak activations on recalled 1 tokens. Even with all the conditions, most matching steps do not fire (dev precision 0.24). It looks like a threshold crossing of a graded mix of token identities, not a clean rule.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=d (+3.96), in_tok=1 (+2.96), prev_tok=z (+2.79), phase=2 & in_tok=1 (+2.76), prev_tok=w (+2.62), orig_idx=3 (+2.49). Lower it: recall_idx=4 (-2.27), prev_tok=d (-0.98).
